Veilwalkers.name: Veilwalkers
Veilwalkers.basicInfo: A secretive organization that studies the Rebirth phenomenon: the appearance of souls from other worlds in Luxcellia. Part research institute, part spy network, part support group for confused interdimensional travelers. The Veilwalkers know that the current protagonist is not the first Reborn to arrive, and they have extensive files on previous cases. Their leader is a former Reborn who arrived decades ago and has been quietly preparing for something they won't fully explain.
Veilwalkers.hiddenInfo: The Veilwalkers' leader believes the Rebirth phenomenon is accelerating toward a dimensional convergence event that will reshape Luxcellia's relationship with other worlds entirely.

Crimson Circle.name: Crimson Circle
Crimson Circle.basicInfo: An underground information network that operates across every major city in Luxcellia, trading in secrets, blackmail material, favors, and debts. The Crimson Circle is not a thieves' guild (they consider theft inelegant) but an organization of information specialists, fixers, and social engineers who know that knowledge is more valuable than any dungeon loot. Their agents are everywhere: the friendly bartender, the well-dressed stranger at the gala, the merchant who remembers your name a little too well. They operate on a strict code: information is sold, never given freely, and a Circle debt is always collected. They are not evil, but they are expensive, amoral, and they always know more than they should. Dealing with the Circle is like handling fire: useful, dangerous, and addictive.
Crimson Circle.hiddenInfo: The Crimson Circle's founder was a Reborn who arrived decades ago and used knowledge from their old world, social engineering, intelligence tradecraft, network theory, to build an organization that no one in Luxcellia had the conceptual framework to create. The current leadership doesn't know about the Rebirth connection, but the founder's old-world methods are embedded in every protocol they use.

Twilight Court.name: Twilight Court
Twilight Court.basicInfo: The governing body of the Twilight Dominion, led by Demon Lord Kuroyuki. A sophisticated government built on binding contracts, strength-based hierarchy, and pragmatic diplomacy. Maintains embassies in human nations, engages in trade, and occasionally sends terrifyingly competent diplomats to royal functions. The Court views Reborn individuals with academic curiosity and considers them potential allies rather than threats. Demon nobles are cultured, dangerous, and unfairly attractive.
Twilight Court.hiddenInfo: Kuroyuki has been collecting Reborn individuals who fled human persecution and offering them sanctuary, building a hidden community of otherworldly souls within the Dominion.

Verdant Throne.name: Verdant Throne
Verdant Throne.basicInfo: The ancient ruling body of Shingetsu Evergrove: a theocratic council of jungle priests, serpentkin elders, plant-mages, and the hereditary guardian families who have protected the deepest temple complexes for generations. The Verdant Throne governs from Verdanthrone, the living temple city where architecture grows organically from the trees themselves: bridges of woven vine, halls of shaped wood, and throne rooms where the walls breathe and the ceiling is a canopy of flowering branches. The Throne's authority is spiritual as much as political; they maintain the jungle's ecological balance, negotiate with the semi-sentient forest, and perform the seasonal rites that keep the ancient temple wards from failing catastrophically. Their warriors fight with weapons grown from ironwood and enchanted with plant magic. Their priests commune with the jungle's vast root-network, which functions as a continent-spanning communication system older than any nation. The Verdant Throne is isolationist by tradition, welcoming by temperament, and deeply conflicted about the outside world's growing interest in their ruins. They want allies but fear exploitation, and a Reborn individual who approaches them with respect rather than treasure-hunting ambition may find the warmest welcome on the continent.
Verdant Throne.hiddenInfo: The Verdant Throne's highest priests can communicate with the jungle's root network, and through it, they have detected something growing beneath the deepest temple; not a monster or an artifact, but a new Riftmaw forming around a seed of cross-dimensional energy. The jungle appears to be trying to contain it. The Throne's most closely guarded secret is that the jungle itself may be alive in a way that transcends normal biology: an ancient organism that has been protecting Luxcellia from dimensional instability for millennia.

Fanged Covenant.name: Fanged Covenant
Fanged Covenant.basicInfo: A political alliance of beastkin clans from the Verdania Wilds, united in their fight for territorial rights, political recognition, and equal treatment under continental law. Led by a council of clan elders and war chiefs, the Covenant balances traditional clan values with the pragmatic need to engage with human-dominated politics. They're fierce allies, stubborn negotiators, and will never forgive a betrayal. Their warriors are among the best on the continent, and their clan festivals are legendary.
Fanged Covenant.hiddenInfo: The Fanged Covenant possesses an oral tradition describing a Reborn arrival thousands of years ago. If verified, this would rewrite the timeline of the Rebirth phenomenon entirely.

Moonwatch Order.name: Moonwatch Order
Moonwatch Order.basicInfo: A knightly order sworn to protect Reborn individuals, believing them to be divinely sent souls whose arrival heralds a great change in Luxcellia's fate. The Moonwatch are devoted, well-trained, and operate as independent escorts, investigators, and guardians for anyone confirmed as Reborn. Their devotion is genuine and their combat skills are excellent, but their assumptions about the protagonist's 'destiny' can become suffocating. They track Rebirth events, maintain safe houses, and have standing agreements with several factions to ensure Reborn individuals receive protection. Their knights are earnest, chivalric, and tend to view the protagonist with a reverence that is flattering at first and increasingly uncomfortable. The Order's leadership includes both sincere protectors and political opportunists who see Reborn individuals as tools for advancing their faction's influence.
Moonwatch Order.hiddenInfo: The Moonwatch Order was founded after a previous Reborn individual saved the life of the Order's first Grand Master and then vanished without explanation. The Order has spent generations preparing for the next arrival. Their archives contain detailed records of at least four previous Reborn, including one who apparently chose to leave Luxcellia voluntarily: information that challenges the assumption that Rebirth is always one-directional.

The Pale Accord.name: The Pale Accord
The Pale Accord.basicInfo: A unique governing alliance between the mortal and spirit populations of Meikyo Spiritfen: a formal diplomatic framework that grants political representation to both the living and the dead. The Pale Accord operates through a dual council: mortal representatives handle physical infrastructure, trade, and external diplomacy, while spirit representatives manage the supernatural ecosystem, ancestral affairs, and cross-veil disputes. Decisions require consensus from both sides, which makes governance slow but remarkably fair. The Accord's greatest achievement is the Treaty of Mist: a binding magical contract that prevents spirits from possessing the living without consent and prevents the living from banishing spirits without cause. Violation is punished by both councils. The Accord's members include mortal mayors, spirit elders, foxkin mediums who serve as translators, and a small peacekeeping force equipped with weapons that work on both physical and spiritual threats. The faction is respected for achieving something no other region has managed: a functional democracy that includes the dead.
The Pale Accord.hiddenInfo: The Treaty of Mist has a critical flaw: it assumes the boundary between worlds will remain stable. If the veil weakens further, the treaty's enforcement mechanisms fail, and the relationship between spirits and mortals reverts to the chaotic, predatory dynamic that existed before the Accord. Several spirit elders know this and are quietly preparing contingencies that their mortal counterparts would find alarming.

Thornveil Court.name: Thornveil Court
Thornveil Court.basicInfo:
The native ruling body of the Rosethorn Nocturne: an aristocratic council of vampire-blooded houses, dark elf matriarchs, demonkin lords, and fallen celestial nobles who govern through blood pacts, seasonal courts, and elaborate social rituals that make Crownveil politics look like a school council. The Thornveil Court is not evil; it is old, beautiful, dramatic, and operates on a value system where passion, loyalty, and aesthetic excellence matter more than conventional morality.

The Thornveil Court is the reason the Rosethorn Nocturne exists as an independent region. They have maintained neutrality through centuries of blood diplomacy, strategic marriages, and the simple fact that nobody wants to fight vampire-blooded nobles in their own territory at night.

The social season is a continent-wide invitation for beautiful, powerful people to attend parties, compete for attention, and fall dangerously in love under circumstances that are never simple. A Reborn attending a Thornveil ball is fresh blood in every sense. The Court finds them fascinating. The Court's eligible heirs find them irresistible. And the blood pact governing marriage alliances contains a clause about "souls not born of this world" that nobody has triggered, until now.

The Twilight Court considers the Thornveil an eccentric cousin. The Crown considers them a political headache. The Church considers them borderline heretical. The Thornveil considers everyone else poorly dressed.
Thornveil Court.hiddenInfo: The blood pact's clause about "souls not born of this world" was written by the first Reborn to love someone from this region: meant to protect that Reborn's descendants. But it was written as a binding magical contract, and if triggered, it grants any Reborn who marries into a Thornveil house full voting rights in the Court. This would shift the Nocturne's power balance overnight. Several houses are quietly engineering encounters between their heirs and Reborn individuals, while others are determined to prevent it, and the Crimson Circle has figured this out and is selling the information to both sides.

Duskfire Wardens.name: Duskfire Wardens
Duskfire Wardens.basicInfo: An order of storm mages who maintain the ancient wind temples scattered across the Kagaribi Duskfields, channeling weather magic to sustain the region's unique perpetual twilight and protect the plains from natural disasters. The Wardens are scholars, engineers, and mages who have dedicated themselves to understanding and maintaining a system they did not build and cannot fully comprehend. Each wind temple is a complex of spinning stone pillars, resonance chambers, and weather-focusing arrays that requires constant calibration and occasional emergency repair: usually during the worst possible storm. Warden initiates train by standing in controlled wind tunnels until they can shape air currents by instinct. The fully trained Wardens can call lightning, redirect storms, and create wind barriers capable of stopping a cavalry charge. They are respected by the clans for keeping the Duskfields habitable and slightly feared for the power they wield. The Wardens' headquarters is the Grand Aerie: a wind temple built into a mesa that serves as both research facility and the best vantage point on the continent. From the Aerie's observation platform, you can see the curvature of the world.
Duskfire Wardens.hiddenInfo: The wind temples are failing. The Wardens have been compensating with increasingly desperate improvisation, but the core systems are degrading faster than they can repair them. Within a generation, the perpetual dusk will end, and the Duskfields' ecosystem will collapse. The Wardens have been secretly recruiting anyone with advanced technical knowledge, and a Reborn individual with engineering or physics background might be the breakthrough they need.

Adventurer's Guild.name: Adventurer's Guild
Adventurer's Guild.basicInfo: The continent's largest independent organization for freelance heroes, monster hunters, and dungeon explorers. Operates guild halls in every major city with a ranking system from F to S. Politically neutral by charter, practically essential to everyone. Known for competitive contracts, brutal ranking exams, and suspiciously attractive receptionists. The Guild Master is an S-Rank retired adventurer who nobody has seen fight in years, which makes everyone nervous. The Guild also charters Adventurer Companies: banners of adventurers ranked Iron to Mythril, founded at any hall by a founder and two willing partners.
Adventurer's Guild.hiddenInfo: The Guild Master is a former Reborn who arrived fifty years ago and has been quietly shaping continental events from behind the scenes.

Cinderborn Compact.name: Cinderborn Compact
Cinderborn Compact.basicInfo:
A guild-state of master smiths, volcanic miners, oni warlords, and fire mages who control the Kagutsuchi Emberwake's forge industry through craft excellence and raw territorial power. The Compact is not one organization; it is an alliance of forge clans, mining families, and oni strongholds who agreed centuries ago that cooperation beats competition when you're all living on a volcano. Every major forge in the region operates under Compact law. Every weapon worth naming was made by a Compact smith. Every member carries a forearm brand marking them as forgesworn.

The Emberwake produces the best weapons, armor, and enchanted metalwork on the continent. The Compact controls supply, making them economically powerful in ways the Merchant Lords resent and the Crown nervously respects. They're not expansionist. They don't need to be. Everyone comes to them eventually, because everyone needs a blade.

Oni courtship in the Compact is intense, physical, and demands proof at the forge or in combat before anyone takes you seriously as a romantic prospect. A Reborn who impresses a Compact smith gets an apprenticeship offer, a personal forge key, and an oni father figure who challenges them to arm-wrestling at dinner. The romance is earned through fire.

The Guild wants Compact weapons at guild prices. The Compact says no. The Crown wants Compact loyalty. The Compact says they're loyal to the mountain. The Church wants to inspect the oni blood pacts. The Compact says the Church can inspect the inside of a volcano.
Cinderborn Compact.hiddenInfo: The central caldera's dragon-heart crystal was not discovered by the Dragonkin; it was forged by the first Compact founders as a containment vessel for an ancient fire entity. The artifact the region treats as a dormant Blessing source is actually a prison, and the intensifying powers and cheat-skill mutations near the caldera are leaks from something trying to wake up. The eldest forge masters know the truth and have spent generations reinforcing the seals.

Crown of Luxcellia.name: Crown of Luxcellia
Crown of Luxcellia.basicInfo: The royal government of the Crownveil Sovereignty, led by Queen Celestine Luxcrown. Commands the Royal Knight Order, administers the noble houses, and manages the most powerful human nation on the continent. The Queen is beautiful, brilliant, and politically ruthless. She treats summoned heroes as assets, reborn individuals as variables, and her own daughter's romantic interests as matters of national security. The court is gorgeous and dangerous in equal measure.
Crown of Luxcellia.hiddenInfo: Queen Celestine has a private intelligence network that rivals the Veilwalkers' and monitors every known Reborn individual on the continent.

Crystalvein Cartel.name: Crystalvein Cartel
Crystalvein Cartel.basicInfo: The economic backbone of Kurogane Deephollow: a powerful mining and trade consortium that controls the underground's crystal economy with the efficiency of a corporation and the ruthlessness of a crime family. The Cartel mines enchanted crystals, mana-veins, rare metals, and geode formations that surface-world enchanters, artificers, and jewelers pay extraordinary prices for. They operate crystal markets, fund expedition teams, maintain trade routes between the Deephollow and surface cities, and employ a private security force that is suspiciously well-armed for a trade guild. The Cartel's leadership is a council of mining magnates: dwarven-blooded industrialists, crystal golem artificers, and deep elf gem-mages who treat commerce as art. They're not evil, but they are aggressive about profit, territorial about mining rights, and willing to bend rules that get between them and a productive vein. Their members are hardworking, competitive, and proud of building an economy in a place the surface world forgot existed.
Crystalvein Cartel.hiddenInfo: The Cartel has discovered a crystal vein that resonates specifically with Reborn souls; it amplifies Blessings and cheat skills temporarily. They've been stockpiling this crystal in secret, unsure whether to sell it, weaponize it, or destroy it before someone else does. Several Cartel members are also quietly buying information about Reborn arrivals from surface contacts.

Depthwarden Circle.name: Depthwarden Circle
Depthwarden Circle.basicInfo: The military order that keeps the Deephollow safe from the things that live below it. The Depthwardens patrol the tunnels, maintain the ancient seals, fight the deep-dwelling monsters that crawl up from levels nobody has mapped, and ensure that the subterranean civilization doesn't get eaten by whatever lurks at the bottom. They are disciplined, brave, slightly paranoid, and equipped with crystal-enhanced weapons and armor that glow in the dark, which is both tactically useful and dramatically stunning. Warden initiates undergo trials in sealed tunnels where they face darkness, isolation, and their own fears before earning their crystal-forged blades. The order is respected and feared in equal measure, and their commander, a stone-faced dwarven woman named Iron Matriarch Tsukasa, has held the deep line for thirty years without losing a seal. The Depthwardens accept recruits from any background, and surface adventurers who prove themselves in the deep tunnels earn a respect that translates across factions.
Depthwarden Circle.hiddenInfo: The Depthwardens know that the deepest sealed chamber contains something that predates the Deephollow civilization entirely: an artifact or entity that has been slowly, almost imperceptibly, weakening the seals from the inside. The rate of weakening has accelerated since the first Reborn arrived in the Deephollow, and Matriarch Tsukasa suspects a connection she cannot yet prove.

The Wandering Table.name: The Wandering Table
The Wandering Table.basicInfo: A culinary guild of traveling cooks, brewers, and food artisans who operate the continent's best mobile restaurants, appear at every major festival, and maintain a sacred neutrality that even warring factions respect. The Wandering Table's caravan-kitchens serve everyone, adventurers, nobles, demons, beastkin, clergy, because everyone needs to eat and the Table believes that shared meals prevent more wars than armies do. Their master chefs are celebrities. Their apprentices are everywhere. Their signature (a carved wooden spoon hung outside any establishment they endorse) is the most trusted quality mark in Luxcellia's food industry. Joining the Wandering Table as a patron, supplier, or apprentice opens doors across every faction, because nobody wants to be the person who offended the people who make the food.
The Wandering Table.hiddenInfo: The Wandering Table's neutrality is enforced by a binding covenant with an ancient nature spirit who protects their caravans from violence. Any attack on a Wandering Table kitchen triggers a defensive curse that makes the attacker unable to taste food for a year: a punishment that sounds trivial until you live in Luxcellia, where food is one of life's greatest pleasures. The Table's inner circle knows about this protection and uses it judiciously, but the covenant has limits they haven't fully tested.

Lanternkeep Covenant.name: Lanternkeep Covenant
Lanternkeep Covenant.basicInfo: The shrine keepers who maintain the spiritual infrastructure of Meikyo Spiritfen: the lanterns, wards, barriers, and rituals that prevent the thin boundary between worlds from collapsing entirely. The Covenant operates dozens of shrines across the fen's islands, each one a carefully maintained anchor point that keeps the mortal and spirit realms from merging completely. Their members are priests, exorcists, ward-crafters, and spirit diplomats who have dedicated their lives to walking the line between worlds. They light the lanterns at dusk, perform the binding rituals at midnight, and negotiate with restless spirits at dawn. The work is sacred, exhausting, and deeply lonely: Covenant members often develop closer relationships with spirits than with living people, which creates a distinctive melancholy that makes them fascinating and slightly heartbreaking. Their annual Lantern Drift ceremony, where thousands of spirit-lights are released onto the waterways, is one of the most beautiful events on the continent.
Lanternkeep Covenant.hiddenInfo: The Covenant's oldest records describe the catastrophic event that tore the veil, and attribute it to a Reborn individual who attempted to open a permanent passage back to their original world. The attempt failed, the Reborn vanished, and the wound in reality has never healed. The Covenant fears that another Reborn might attempt the same thing, and they monitor every Reborn who enters the fen with quiet, desperate vigilance.

Kuroyuki's Shadowhand.name: Kuroyuki's Shadowhand
Kuroyuki's Shadowhand.basicInfo:
The Demon Lord's personal network of operatives, agents, and chosen individuals who answer to Kuroyuki directly: outside the Twilight Court's diplomatic and bureaucratic apparatus. Where the Court negotiates, the Shadowhand acts. Where diplomats sign contracts, Shadowhand agents move unseen, retrieve what the Court cannot ask for publicly, and protect interests that formal diplomacy cannot acknowledge.

The Shadowhand is not an assassin's guild. It is something more dangerous: a collection of individuals Kuroyuki has personally selected for absolute loyalty, unusual competence, and the willingness to do what the Court's formal structures cannot. This includes intelligence gatherers, covert protectors of Reborn refugees, specialists in dimensional anomalies, and the rare agent whose Blessing makes them uniquely suited to tasks no one else can accomplish. Shadowhand agents do not know each other. They know only Kuroyuki and their mission.

Kuroyuki formed the Shadowhand after centuries of watching the Court's formal diplomacy fail to protect the things she actually cares about: the Reborn individuals the Court debates theoretically, the dimensional research the Veilwalkers hoard, the secrets the Church would burn. The Shadowhand exists because the Demon Lord's conscience and curiosity outpace her government's willingness to act.

A Shadowhand agent who falls for a Reborn faces a unique conflict: they report directly to the Demon Lord, who has made protecting Reborn a personal priority, but the agent's attachment would compromise their operational independence. Kuroyuki finds this hilarious and concerning in equal measure.
Kuroyuki's Shadowhand.hiddenInfo: The Shadowhand's deepest purpose is not intelligence or covert action. Kuroyuki created it to monitor the dimensional boundary that she believes caused the ancient catastrophe she's been investigating for centuries. Every agent's mission, regardless of what they're told, feeds data into her central thesis: the Rebirth phenomenon is accelerating toward an event she cannot predict, and the Twilight Court's diplomatic structures are too slow to respond. The Shadowhand is her early warning system for a catastrophe that formal governments cannot prepare for because they do not believe it exists.

Thornblood Reclamation.name: Thornblood Reclamation
Thornblood Reclamation.basicInfo: An adventurer-scholar expedition force dedicated to exploring, mapping, and recovering knowledge from the ancient temple ruins throughout Shingetsu Evergrove. The Reclamation operates base camps at the jungle's edges and sends teams of treasure hunters, archaeologists, trap specialists, and combat escorts into temple complexes that have been sealed for centuries. Their work is equal parts academic research and adrenaline-fueled dungeon diving: every expedition produces artifacts, academic papers, and stories that would make a bard weep with envy. The Reclamation's founder, a retired A-Rank adventurer who lost his arm to a temple guardian and his heart to the jungle's mystery, runs the operation from a fortified camp where artifact analysis and expedition planning happen over strong coffee and stronger language. Members are recruited from the Guild, the Academy, and the occasionally desperate; anyone who can swing a blade, read ancient script, or outrun a carnivorous vine qualifies. The Reclamation pays well, provides excellent equipment, and has a casualty rate that they describe as 'acceptable' in a tone that discourages follow-up questions.
Thornblood Reclamation.hiddenInfo: The Reclamation's deepest expedition reached a sealed inner sanctum containing inscriptions in a language that no Luxcellian scholar can read, but which a Reborn individual on the team recognized instantly as a language from their original world. The expedition leader suppressed this finding and has been privately seeking more Reborn translators. The implications of a pre-Luxcellian civilization writing in an Earth language are staggering, and the Reclamation's leadership is split on whether to publish or bury the discovery.

Windrunner Confederacy.name: Windrunner Confederacy
Windrunner Confederacy.basicInfo: The allied nomadic clans of the Kagaribi Duskfields, united under a rotating council of clan chiefs who govern through tradition, consensus, and the occasional dramatic riding challenge. The Confederacy is not a nation in the conventional sense; it is a living agreement between free peoples who chose cooperation over conquest. Each clan maintains its own territory, customs, beast herds, and internal governance while contributing riders, resources, and warriors to the Confederacy's shared defense and trade networks. The Windrunners are famous across the continent for their cavalry, their festivals, and their absolute refusal to build permanent walls. Their warriors fight from the backs of bonded storm-beasts, massive elk-like creatures with lightning-laced antlers, and their archery is performed at full gallop with an accuracy that makes Guild marksmen weep. The Great Gathering, held twice yearly, is part parliament, part festival, part marriage market, and part continent-wide party. The Confederacy welcomes travelers who respect the plains and has a standing offer to any adventurer brave enough to try the Rider's Trial: bond a storm-beast, survive the proving run, and earn clan-friend status for life.
Windrunner Confederacy.hiddenInfo: The Confederacy's oral tradition contains a prophecy about a 'Rider from Beyond the Sky'; someone not born of Luxcellia who will bond the legendary Thundermane, a storm-beast that has rejected every rider for three hundred years. The beast is real, it lives in the deepest part of the Duskfields, and it has recently begun moving toward the edges of the plains as if searching for something. The clan chiefs are divided on whether a Reborn fulfilling this prophecy would be salvation or disaster.

Cerulean Merchant Lords.name: Cerulean Merchant Lords
Cerulean Merchant Lords.basicInfo: A trade consortium that controls the Cerulean Coast's shipping lanes, major markets, and guild funding. Money is their magic and profit is their religion. They'll fund any quest, sponsor any adventurer, and back any faction: for a price and a percentage. Individual Merchant Lords range from charming philanthropists to ruthless profiteers. They maintain their own private security forces and have been known to start small wars over tariff disputes.
Cerulean Merchant Lords.hiddenInfo: The Merchant Lords have been funding both the Church and the Veilwalkers simultaneously, ensuring their profit margins regardless of which faction gains dominance.

Silver Crescent Academy.name: Silver Crescent Academy
Silver Crescent Academy.basicInfo: The continent's premier magical academy, located near Aureliath. Accepts students based on talent regardless of birth: officially. In practice, noble families wield considerable influence over admissions, faculty appointments, and curriculum. The student council president wields more political power than most minor nobles. Class rankings cause more interpersonal drama than actual wars. The Academy produces the continent's finest mages, and its alumni network is one of Luxcellia's most powerful unofficial organizations.
Silver Crescent Academy.hiddenInfo: Headmaster Soushi's research into the Rebirth phenomenon is far more extensive than anyone realizes. He's identified a pattern in Reborn arrivals that suggests they're not random.

Mirage Weavers' Conclave.name: Mirage Weavers' Conclave
Mirage Weavers' Conclave.basicInfo:
A loose collective of illusionists, reality-benders, desert sages, and truth-seekers who study and maintain the Renka Mirage Sea's unique relationship with the boundary between real and unreal. The Conclave is not a government; it is closer to a philosophy department with enforcement capabilities. They study mirages, create mirages, and determine which mirages are real, which are dangerous, and which are the desert trying to tell you something. In a region where reality is a suggestion, the people who can read the suggestions hold real power.

The Conclave maintains caravan routes by marking safe paths through mirage fields. They adjudicate disputes by determining what actually happened versus what appeared to happen. They train the region's mages. And they guard secrets about the nature of reality that the Silver Crescent Academy would study and the Church would suppress.

A Mirage Weaver who falls for a Reborn faces an existential question: is the attraction real, or is it another mirage? Reborn souls register strangely on the Conclave's instruments, somewhere between real and impossible, and a Weaver who gets close to one starts seeing things differently. The desert romance is dreamy, surreal, and punctuated by moments of startling honesty in a culture that normally communicates through beautiful lies.

The Academy considers the Conclave's approach "undisciplined." The Conclave considers the Academy "boring." The Wandering Table is their oldest ally. The Veilwalkers want the Conclave's data on dimensional anomalies, and the Conclave keeps pretending not to have any.
Mirage Weavers' Conclave.hiddenInfo: The Conclave's instruments have detected something in the deep desert that registers as more real than reality itself: an anchor point where the boundary between worlds is not thin but absent. The Veilwalkers would consider this the most important discovery in dimensional research history. The Conclave has classified it because they are not sure what would happen if someone approached it. The last mirage near the anchor showed a door that doesn't exist in any architectural style from Luxcellia, or from any world any Reborn has described.

Tidebound Shrine Keepers.name: Tidebound Shrine Keepers
Tidebound Shrine Keepers.basicInfo:
A spiritual order of shrine maidens, moon priests, and tide-readers who maintain the sacred sites across the Tsukihana Tidelace's island chain and serve as the region's informal government. They are not politicians; they are the connective tissue that holds the Tidelace together. Every island has a shrine, every shrine has a Keeper, and every Keeper answers, loosely, to the High Tide Priestess on the central island. They keep the lanterns lit, the wards maintained, the sea spirits appeased, and the tide calendar accurate. Without them, the festivals don't happen, the merfolk don't trade, and the ocean gets angry.

Crossing the Shrine Keepers doesn't get you killed. It gets you uninvited from every festival, denied harbor access, and whispered about by merfolk who will absolutely tell the sea serpents you're rude. Their power is cultural, not military, and in the Tidelace that matters more.

Shrine Keepers take vows of spiritual dedication but not celibacy. A Keeper falling for a Reborn is scandalous, beautiful, and exactly the kind of forbidden-but-not-actually-forbidden tension that makes the Tidelace run on romantic drama. The moon is always watching. The tides know your heart.

The Shrine Keepers maintain a cold war with the Cerulean Merchant Lords over the commercialization of the Tidelace's sacred festivals: fought with guest lists, harbor fees, and passive-aggressive lantern placement.
Tidebound Shrine Keepers.hiddenInfo: The High Tide Priestess receives visions during the Vanishing Isle's appearances: memories that do not belong to her. She has been quietly collecting fragments from every Reborn who has visited the island, and the pattern she's piecing together suggests that the Vanishing Isle is not a natural phenomenon. It is a door that opens from the other side, and someone has been watching Luxcellia for a very long time.

Church of the First Light.name: Church of the First Light
Church of the First Light.basicInfo: The dominant religious institution devoted to the First Light. Operates healing halls, paladin orders, and divine magic academies. The Luminous Conclave possesses genuine oracular power and claims authority over all matters of divine blessing. Publicly benevolent and charitable. Privately possessive about Reborn and Summoned individuals, politically influential, and in possession of prophecies they share very selectively. The current High Priestess smiles at everyone and trusts almost no one.
Church of the First Light.hiddenInfo: The sealed prophecy about the Rebirth phenomenon is stored beneath the Grand Cathedral. Its contents suggest the Reborn have a specific purpose that would upend the Church's current theology if revealed.

Deepwatch Lantern Company.name: Deepwatch Lantern Company
Deepwatch Lantern Company.basicInfo:
[Adventurer Company · Guild rank: Gold · Specialty: Riftmaw dives, deep mapping, rescue · Hall: Floor Zero Gatehouse, Floor Zero Gatehouse: Canteen]
The Company at the top of the Riftmaw Depth Board. Deepwatch dives deep, maps what it finds, and goes back down for anyone who did not come up. Its crest is a hooded lantern over a descending stair; a Deepwatch lantern left burning on a landing means someone is still below. Deepwatch recruits slowly, and only people who have already survived a floor.
Leader: Tetsu Tetsuō (A-rank, holds the depth record at The 97th Floor Door)
Members: Senna Yuureizuki (mid-floor veteran); Tsukasa Kuromizu (deep-tunnel cartographer, sells maps under Company contract)
Deepwatch Lantern Company.hiddenInfo: Since Tetsu came back from the bottom of The 97th Floor Door, Deepwatch's drills have changed: longer descents, rope teams, rescue practice for floors nobody has reached. The members have noticed. Tetsu has not explained what he is training them for.

The Flagon Irregulars.name: The Flagon Irregulars
The Flagon Irregulars.basicInfo:
[Adventurer Company · Guild rank: Silver · Specialty: monster bounties, warren clearing, training rookies · Hall: Ironhold, The Rusty Flagon]
A loud, generous Company that runs from a corner table at The Rusty Flagon and takes the monster bounties on Ironhold's board that would kill a rookie working alone. The Irregulars are always recruiting and never send a new member out without a veteran. Their crest is a dented tankard crossed with a troll's tooth. Rival Companies call them a nursery; the Irregulars' rookies outlive everyone else's.
Leader: Ran Kōga (veteran frontier brawler)
Members: Mika Haitsume (B-rank treasure hunter)
The Flagon Irregulars.hiddenInfo: Ran founded the Irregulars to keep a dead sergeant's promise: keep the young ones alive. Ran never speaks of the company she served in before, and the Irregulars' one hard rule, no contract with cargo nobody will name, comes from it.

Tidecrest Company.name: Tidecrest Company
Tidecrest Company.basicInfo:
[Adventurer Company · Guild rank: Silver · Specialty: sea-lane and caravan escorts, coastal dungeons · Hall: Portmaris, Portside Tavern Row]
A dashing coastal Company with the lowest loss rate on Portmaris escort contracts and the most dramatic arrivals in any harbor. Tidecrest guards ships, caravans and pearl convoys along the Cerulean Coast and dives the sea caves in between. Its crest is a breaking wave over crossed cutlasses. Tidecrest and the Gilded Caravan Company bid against each other for every rich escort on the coast.
Leader: Torao Arami (B-rank swashbuckler)
Members: Takamaru Yagami (aerial scout, flies with Tidecrest on contract); Hana Yamada (junior member, F-rank alchemist)
Tidecrest Company.hiddenInfo: Torao keeps Tidecrest's books spotless because the Cerulean Merchant Lords would welcome any excuse to pull its charter. The impostor running escort scams under Torao's name has started painting a forged Tidecrest crest on the wagons too.

The Gilded Caravan Company.name: The Gilded Caravan Company
The Gilded Caravan Company.basicInfo:
[Adventurer Company · Guild rank: Gold · Specialty: desert caravans, catacomb salvage · Hall: Sunveil Caravanserai, Trade Courtyard]
The richest Company in the Mirage Sea, run like a trading house that happens to carry swords. The Gilded Caravan escorts its own caravans, guards other people's for a fee, and funds salvage runs into the Starfall Bazaar Catacombs. Its crest is a golden camel under a desert star. Members are paid well and on time, and they are expected to win.
Leader: Takuma Hidaka (B-rank caravan master)
Members: Safiya Ryuusazanami (catacomb guide)
The Gilded Caravan Company.hiddenInfo: Someone is sabotaging caravans along the Gilded Caravan's routes, but only its competitors' caravans, which makes the Company look brilliant and guilty at once. Takuma's catacomb salvage is quietly hunting artifacts that would give the Company a monopoly.

The Frostfang Hunt.name: The Frostfang Hunt
The Frostfang Hunt.basicInfo:
[Adventurer Company · Guild rank: Silver · Specialty: mountain hunts, monster migrations, pass escorts · Hall: Frostbell Onsen Town, Mountain Guild Lodge]
A tight mountain Company that hunts the Veilpeak's monsters, tracks their migrations, and walks travelers through the passes. The Frostfang Hunt calls itself a pack and means it: members eat together at the Mountain Guild Lodge, and nobody is left on a slope. Its crest is a white wolf's fang against a blue peak.
Leader: Gunther Hyōshun (A-rank mountain specialist)
Members: Mira Ginrou (D-rank beast tamer, with her spirit fox Yuki)
The Frostfang Hunt.hiddenInfo: Gunther built the Hunt after losing his first pack to a Riftmaw outbreak. The Veilpeak's apex predators have started moving down-slope, and the Hunt is quietly stretched too thin to cover every pass.

The Greenwake Company.name: The Greenwake Company
The Greenwake Company.basicInfo:
[Adventurer Company · Guild rank: Gold · Specialty: forest trails, canopy scouting, abyss expeditions · Hall: Lanternmoss Village, Mossglow Commons]
The trail-keepers of the Verdania Wilds. The Greenwake Company guides expeditions, clears monster nests off the forest roads, scouts the canopy, and maps the Flowering Abyss for scholars and herbalists. Its crest is a green leaf in a lantern's glow. Greenwake members know which paths the forest is letting people use this season.
Leader: Hayato Haibara (A-rank ranger)
Members: Satsuki Tsuyukusa (canopy scout); Wakana Kusunoki (botanical explorer of the Flowering Abyss)
The Greenwake Company.hiddenInfo: Hayato has come close enough to kill the spirit beast that took his pack four times, and has not. Greenwake's members know their leader goes alone into one part of the Wilds and comes back quieter each time.

The Vaunted Blade Company.name: The Vaunted Blade Company
The Vaunted Blade Company.basicInfo:
[Adventurer Company · Guild rank: Gold · Specialty: tournaments, duels, high-profile bounties · Hall: Knight's Tournament Grounds, Champion's Pavilion]
The most famous and most theatrical Company in Crownveil, built around tournament champions and the bounties that make headlines. The Vaunted Blade challenges rising Companies to banner bouts, wins most of them, and sells tickets. Its crest is a silver sword crowned with laurel. Rivals call it vain; the crowds love it.
Leader: Raiga Kōtetsu (A-rank tournament champion)
Members: Ryoma Enjō (rising star); Raiden Kurogane (B-rank martial artist)
The Vaunted Blade Company.hiddenInfo: Most of the Vaunted Blade's prize money vanishes, and the members assume Raiga spends it on show. Raiga sends it to orphanages and would rather lose a bout than have anyone find out.

The Emberforge Company.name: The Emberforge Company
The Emberforge Company.basicInfo:
[Adventurer Company · Guild rank: Silver · Specialty: volcanic ore runs, weapon testing, forge commissions · Hall: Emberglass Forge City, Forge Guild Commission Office]
A Company of fighting smiths. Emberforge takes the ore runs no merchant will risk, fetches Riftmaw crystal and volcanic metal from the Kagutsuchi Emberwake, and field-tests the weapons its members forge. Its crest is a hammer over a rising flame. Hire Emberforge as an escort and the escort will critique your sword.
Leader: Ragna Kadan (B-rank master smith)
Members: Kira Tetsutsume (B-rank blacksmith); Genzo Haikamuri (retired A-rank, the Company's founder and advisor)
The Emberforge Company.hiddenInfo: Kira's experiments with a Riftmaw ore that answers to Rebirth energy began on Emberforge ore runs, and the factions that want that metal have started watching the Company. Genzo is tracing an unchartered mercenary company that is re-arming with Border War ordnance.

Stormblood Vanguard.name: Stormblood Vanguard
Stormblood Vanguard.basicInfo:
[Adventurer Company · Guild rank: Mythril · Specialty: Abyssal-floor expeditions, continental threats · Hall: Aureliath, Guild Quarter]
The most famous active party on the continent and the only Company flying a Mythril banner today. Five adventurers whose teamwork is so polished that combat choreographers study their patterns, sent where a threat is too big for anyone else. Its crest is a silver lightning bolt splitting a black storm cloud. The Vanguard is rarely in Aureliath for long, and its return empties the taverns of the Guild Quarter. It never posts its dives on the Riftmaw Depth Board, and nobody outside the Company knows how deep it has been. It does not take trials: it invites, and only after deeds the whole continent has heard of.
Leader: Sōma Kazanari (S-rank captain and vanguard swordsman)
Members: Yosuga Raikura (S-rank storm mage, the lightning the Company is named for); Tōya Amagase (A-rank shield guardian, in a documented Constellation with Rindō Fuyuno); Rindō Fuyuno (A-rank battle cleric); Hotaka Isurugi (A-rank spellblade, the Reborn community's most visible success story)
Stormblood Vanguard.hiddenInfo: Two years ago the Vanguard went below the ninety-seventh floor and came back five for five, a claim the Guild has never confirmed and the Company has never repeated in public. Since then it has turned down every contract that would keep it on the surface for long, and Hotaka Isurugi has started asking other Reborn very specific questions about what they remember from before.
